title: Ops efficiency trigger matrix: headcount vs pricing levers (rolling forecast)
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

This working sheet maps utilization and revenue triggers to specific operational levers: hiring cadence, pricing nudges, commitment to Dedicated capacity, and short-term cost actions. Goal: produce an actionable rolling forecast that finance + product + SRE can use for auto-trigger decisions (manual ops today, automation later).

Key outputs (draft):
- Trigger matrix (utilization / revenue / gross margin thresholds -> action items).
- 12-month headcount phasing by function under three baseline scenarios (Base growth, Slower growth, Upside adoption).
- Price sensitivity buckets showing impact on revenue, net burn and runway (fast approximate model).

ASSUMPTIONS (high level, rough):
- Average price per 1k tokens (effective blended, post-discounts): $0.036 (base).
- Variable infra cost per 1k tokens: $0.009 (includes GPU time, caching benefits averaged).
- Token growth scenarios: Base (35% YoY), Slow (15% YoY), Upside (65% YoY).
- Hiring ramp assumptions: 4 new engineers / qtr in base; reduced to 1 / qtr in slow; 6 / qtr in upside.
- Dedicated commitments reduce per-token infra by ~18% but require 3-month notice and 20% minimum utilization ramp.
- Pricing elasticity: small-step changes (+10% or -10%) change demand by -6% / +6% respectively (assumption to validate).

ROLLING FORECAST (condensed table, quarterly):
Columns: Q4-2025 | Q1-2026 | Q2-2026 | Q3-2026 | Q4-2026
Base tokens (B): 1.2 | 1.35 | 1.45 | 1.65 | 1.80
Revenue (k): 43.2 | 48.6 | 52.2 | 59.4 | 64.8
Infra cost (k): 10.8 | 12.2 | 13.1 | 14.9 | 16.2
Gross margin %: 75% | 75% | 75% | 75% | 75%
Net burn impact (scenario): see sensitivity section below.

HEADCOUNT PHASING (by function, cumulative):
- Eng (prod + infra + sqe): Q4-2025 = 58 | Q4-2026 = 74 (base)
- SRE/Platform: Q4-2025 = 12 | Q4-2026 = 16 (base)
- Finance & Ops: Q4-2025 = 8 | Q4-2026 = 10 (base)
- Sales & CS: Q4-2025 = 20 | Q4-2026 = 28 (base, includes expanded AE coverage)
Notes: Phasing is front-loaded in Q1-Q2 for infra hires to support model onboarding; hiring freezes apply in slow scenario if triggers fire.

TRIGGER MATRIX (operationalized rules - DRAFT):
Trigger A: 7-day rolling utilization < 58% of provisioned capacity for > 3 weeks OR Gross margin < 68% -> Action: Pause non-essential hires for 8 weeks; evaluate Dedicated commitment cancellation; implement temporary cost cap (no spot expansion).
Trigger B: 7-day rolling utilization 58-72% (stable) AND revenue growth < 5% q/q -> Action: Slow hiring to 50% planned rate; push pricing tier review to product for small adjustment (+5% on low-volume tiers).
Trigger C: 7-day rolling utilization > 85% for > 2 weeks AND latency SLO stable -> Action: Approve burst purchases for Dedicated; accelerate hiring (+50% for infra); re-evaluate batching and cache thresholds for higher throughput.
Trigger D (price elasticity test): If a +10% price increase yields < 4% drop in demand over 2 weeks, consider permanent +5% uplift on targeted enterprise segments.

PRICING SENSITIVITY (quick scenarios):
Scenario table (Base vs -10% price vs +15% price) for annualized view (approx):
- Base price: Revenue $2.2M, Infra cost $0.55M, Gross profit $1.65M, Delta runway +0.0 months (baseline)
- -10% price: Revenue $1.98M (-10%), Infra cost $0.495M (assuming volume +6% so infra +6%), Gross profit $1.485M, Runway -0.9 months
- +15% price: Revenue $2.53M (+15%), Infra cost $0.517M (assume volume -9%), Gross profit $2.013M, Runway +1.6 months
Interpretation: Small price moves materially affect runway when combined with headcount commitments; discounting to accelerate adoption must be balanced with committed infra purchased (Dedicated).

SENSITIVITY BY HEADCOUNT (toy model):
- Each additional 10 engineers (avg fully-burdened $220k) increases fixed burn by ~+$550k/year.
- To justify 10 eng hires from revenue only, we need incremental gross profit > $550k/year => either ~15% price uplift or ~40% token growth under current gross margins (back-of-envelope).

ACTION ITEMS (near-term):
1) Finance to produce a versioned spreadsheet with per-customer token buckets and margin by route (assign to Priya) - due 2025-11-03.
2) Product to run a 2-week price elasticity A/B on low-volume tier (+10%) and report conversion delta (owner: Ethan) - start 2025-11-10.
3) SRE to create a dashboard widget for 7-day rolling utilization and automated alert (owner: Claire) - due 2025-11-17.
4) Leadership: agree on a hard hiring freeze policy mapping to Trigger A (board briefing required) - tentatively 2025-11-24.

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS (notes to self):
- Elasticity assumptions are weak: MVP A/B required. Historical data noisy due to credits and promo bundles.
- Dedicated capacity contract terms vary by region; need legal review on break terms (possible 90-day notice + 30% early exit).
- Impact of caching and batching improvements not fully captured; could lower infra cost per token by another 6-10% in 3 months if new kernel rollout succeeds.

APPENDIX (quick math snippets):
- Effective blended price calc: (list price * mix) - discounts = $0.036 / 1k tokens (base)
- Breakeven hires calc: hire_cost_annual / incremental_gross_profit_per_hire ~ months to breakeven.

NOTES / VERSION HISTORY:
- v0.1 (2025-10-20) initial draft (Michael Chen)
- v0.2 (2025-11-05) added headcount phasing by function (Priya)
- v0.3 (2026-02-15) updated elasticity numbers after A/B pilot (Ethan)

CONTEXT LINKS:
- See linked artifacts for finance model and PR with the simple calculator.

-- end of working doc --

(Informal: this is intentionally concise — downstream sheet will have row-level customer cohorts, cadence triggers and the boolean logic for automated Slack alerts.)
